meta.title: Sector Rotation
meta.data_note: Rotation from NSE sectoral indices (2026-08-27); per-sector reads from cached bodies, each dated inline

cover.headline: Money is in hard assets and value — Metal, PSU Banks and Pharma lead on the year, while the old defensives, FMCG and IT, are the deepest laggards. The actionable edge is where a sector is turning, not where it already led: IT services are rotating back before the ER&D sub-cohort has, and private banks lead on tape while their margins compress.

coverage.lede: Rotation first, names second. Sectors are ranked by relative strength — how each moves against the Nifty, not its absolute return — then classified Leading, Improving, Weakening or Lagging. A sector that is Improving is where fresh money is most actionable; a sector that already Led may be late.
coverage.brief:
Leaders: Metal, PSU Bank, Pharma.
Laggards: Realty, Media, FMCG, IT.
Actionable turn: broad IT rotating

Policy is a headline feed — a duty or reform is named, its mechanism and effective date are a data gap unless a document supplies them.

lenses.name: Private banks
lenses.read: Leading RS and multi-decadal-low GNPA, but a margin-compression quarter and visible rotation toward PSU banks cap the case.

lenses.name: IT ER&D / SDV
lenses.read: A trough forming after OEM engineering-spend cuts; broad IT already turned, the ER&D cohort playing catch-up. Actionable but unconfirmed.

lenses.name: Life insurance
lenses.read: Negative RS on all three windows, lagging even its own parent financials. Money is rotating out; the deep volume KPIs could not be sourced.

deepdives.name: Private Sector Banks
deepdives.title: Leading on tape, compressing on margin
deepdives.lede: The classic early-cycle, rate-sensitive sleeve — running on credit-volume growth, not a rate tailwind. Leading RS and pristine asset quality set against a margin-squeeze quarter and a rotation of preference toward PSU banks.
deepdives.footer: Proxy ^NSEBANK vs ^NSEI, 21/63/126-day windows to 2026-08-21 · KPIs qualitative from news + Tickertape ratios
deepdives.cycle: NIFTY BANK closed 57,762 above its 50-EMA of 57,223 — price confirms the classification. RBI held the repo rate on 2026-08-06, so this leg runs on volume: system credit growth hit an 18.6% two-year high, industrial credit tripled to 19.2% in June.

tailwinds: Credit growth at a two-year high — 18.6% for the June-end fortnight, industrial credit +19.2% (Business Standard/RBI, 2026-07-10/31).
Asset quality at a multi-decadal best — system GNPA 1.8% (RBI Financial Stability Report, 2026-07-01).
headwinds: Margin compression across most of the peer set — HDFC NIM 'at record low', Axis and Kotak NIM slipping (2026-07-18).
Rotation toward PSU over private — NIFTY PSU BANK +21.8% 1Y vs PRIVATE +2.3% (NSE, 2026-08-22).

stance.text: Neutral for new longs — constructive tape and macro, but a margin quarter and PSU rotation cap fresh private-bank exposure.

story.text: Credit is still small relative to the economy and private banks keep taking share from state-owned ones; the story holds for years even through a margin quarter (AR FY26 MD&A, industry structure). ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE.

deepdives.name: IT ER&D / Auto-SDV Services
deepdives.title: A trough forming, cohort playing catch-up
deepdives.lede: The engineering-R&D and software-defined-vehicle services cohort, hit hard by OEMs deferring discretionary engineering spend, is stabilizing. Broad IT (^CNXIT) has already rotated to Leading; this sub-cohort is catching up, not leading — the Improving class the method flags as actionable but unconfirmed.
deepdives.footer: 5-name equal-weight proxy (KPIT, Tata Elxsi, LTTS, Tata Tech, Cyient) vs ^NSEI · a thin basket, single-stock noise flagged
deepdives.cycle: Two cycles intersect — late-cycle IT offshoring and early/mid-cycle auto-OEM engineering capex. Q1 FY27 prints came in 'less bad than feared' and all five names are positive over 1M, suggesting a trough. Broad ^CNXIT RS is already +8.9/+12.0 on 1M/3M — money returns to IT services faster than to this sub-cohort.

tailwinds: Broad IT services already rotating positive — ^CNXIT RS +8.9/+12.0 on 1M/3M; the cohort is starting to catch the bid (all 5 names +2.8% to +14.4% over 1M).
LTTS the one clear positive margin trend — OPM 19% (Jun-26) up from 16% (Sep-25), P/E 28.4, ROCE 26.7%.
headwinds: 3M/6M RS still net negative for 3 of 5 names — the turn is early and unconfirmed on the medium windows.
Tata Technologies' +40% 3M rally carries an event/rumor component (management denied 'material events', Aug 6-7) — treat its RS contribution with caution.

stance.text: Improving — actionable but unconfirmed; size for a forming trough, not a proven turn, and lean to margin-improvers (LTTS) over the deepest cutters.

story.text: Demand rides a capex cycle that is early, not late; capacity additions trail order books (AR FY26 MD&A, outlook). ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE.

deepdives.name: Life Insurance
deepdives.title: Money is rotating out, and the volume KPIs are dark
deepdives.lede: The listed life insurers lag the Nifty on all three windows and lag even their own parent financials sector — a clear rotation out. The honest complication: the industry's real volume metrics (VNB margin, APE growth, persistency) could not be sourced, so this is a tape read, not a fundamentals all-clear.
deepdives.footer: Custom 5-insurer equal-weight basket vs ^NSEI · directional, not an official index · deep KPIs a labelled gap
deepdives.cycle: A hybrid sleeve — rate-sensitive on embedded value, sentiment-sensitive on ULIP flows, with a long-duration penetration-growth thesis underneath. The basket runs 1.7% below its 50-EMA; NIFTY_FIN_SERVICE returned +1.31/+6.41 on 1M/3M, so financials broadly outperform while life-insurance specifically lags its own parent.
tailwinds: LIC's scale — >66% new-business-premium share and 37.8% ROE (screener.in) — and a still-low insurance penetration underpin a long structural runway.
Not uniformly contracting — LIC +10%, Max Financial +5%, HDFC Life +4% still show positive TTM top-line (screener.in).
headwinds: Negative RS on all three windows and price below the 50-EMA — the tape says money is leaving now.
The real volume KPIs — VNB margin, APE growth, persistency — were not retrievable; absence of a bad print is not reassurance.

stance.text: Unfavorable for new longs — the tape is against it and the fundamentals can't be independently confirmed; wait for either an RS turn or a sourced VNB/APE read.

story.text: Grows with nominal GDP; returns are set by consolidation and pricing discipline rather than by demand (AR FY26 MD&A, opportunities and threats). ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE.

drivers.title: What is actually moving the money
drivers.lede: Three forces explain most of this rotation — a value-and-hard-asset bid, a rate cycle on hold, and a fundamentals-vs-tape gap where the tape is leading.
drivers.footer: Each driver is sourced in the per-sector bodies · policy mechanism and quantum remain a labelled gap
drivers.tailwind: A value and hard-asset bid — Metal +45.9%, PSU Bank +26.6% at a 7.8× P/E — is pulling money toward cyclicals and cheap balance sheets, and system credit growth at a two-year high supports the whole lending complex.
drivers.headwind: The old defensives are being sold — FMCG −15.9% and IT −15.9% on the year — and a margin-compression quarter across private banks plus RBI on hold removes the near-term earnings tailwind that would justify chasing the leaders.
drivers.read: Trade the turns, not the leaders. The cleanest edge is a sector that is Improving before the crowd confirms it — broad IT rotating back ahead of the ER&D cohort — while the year's biggest annual gains (Metal, PSU Bank) may already be late in their move.

gaps.title: What this rotation read does not know
gaps.lede: Every RS number cites its window and proxy; every KPI cites its source. A blocked series or an unpulled KPI is a labelled gap, never a guess.

items.text: VNB margin, APE growth and persistency — the industry's real volume metrics — were not retrievable from the allowed sources; the life-insurance read is a tape read, not a fundamentals all-clear.

items.label: POLICY MECHANISM
items.text: Google News RSS names that a duty or reform moved; the mechanism, quantum and effective date are a gap unless a primary document supplies them.

items.label: THIN PROXIES
items.text: The ER&D and life-insurance baskets are 5-name constructed proxies, not real indices — single-stock moves (Tata Tech +40%) can swing the mean; the median basis is used to classify.

gaps.weakest: The weakest link is the fundamentals-vs-tape gap in life insurance: the RS read is clear, but without VNB/APE the deck cannot say whether the selling is a value opportunity or a justified de-rating.
